_comment: Named, real-world-observed degradation shapes for Layer 5's degraded-install detection check (HARNESS-DESIGN.md section 5.2: 'Named degradations, not ad-hoc edits. Each degraded project reproduces a shape actually observed in the audit and carries the citing repo in a docstring, so a fixture cannot drift into testing an imaginary failure.'). Applied via roundtrip.apply_degradation() against an already-set-up reference-shaped project (never against a real product repo). SCOPE NOTE: RC-4's lock-template-collision shape (LI-1: a sha256-identical lock shared by 8 repos) is deliberately NOT included here -- byte-identity across repos is a cross-repo, fleet-wide fact a single project's round-trip cannot observe by definition (one project has no sibling repos to compare against). That check belongs to Layer 4 (lock.template.uniqueness, WP-5's lock.py), not Layer 5.

shapes.name: missing-hook
shapes.description: The enforcement hook is entirely absent -- the universal, machine-wide shape (0 of 58 tabulated repos pass IC-D4-HOOK on this machine).
shapes.citing_evidence: TEST-MATRIX.md IC-D4-HOOK: FAIL 0/58; EXISTING-VERIFICATION.md doctor probe: hooks-registered-in-project=fail, hooks-enforcement-live=fail

shapes.name: half-commands
shapes.description: Only 2 of 7 project commands present -- the dominant 'never updated' bimodal shape (~30 repos stuck at 2/7 on this machine).
shapes.citing_evidence: TEST-MATRIX.md IC-D1-COMMANDS: bimodal 2-command vs 17-command distribution; RT-1 expected-fail-today

shapes.citing_evidence: TEST-MATRIX.md IC-D1-AGENTS named case: TSM/h3 (2 missing -- cpa, ind -- + 3 unowned foreign extras)
